observations: Board/CLI issuance receives actual Actor and repeats current recent native proof inside its original transaction, including success/replay. Configured operators need verified email and passkey proof. Explicit local implicit authority is not MFA and cannot satisfy configured operator proof.

Native password confirmation returns the actual replacement SID. The original settings component validates canonical account/SID and binds confirmation acknowledgement to that exact verified SID, including the reused confirmation-only CLI view.
Confirmation never approves CLI access. The original challenge is re-read and a separate explicit approval sends narrowing expected-user/session headers checked by the server.

Three controlled original failures reproduce lost recent-auth guidance across a same-session read, unmounted native confirmation across its own session refresh, and cross-account HTTP request coalescing. Final tests pass all three, with late source changes withheld and no automatic approval.

CLI connect uses the exact approved key. Named CLI issuance creates a new human consent challenge rather than reminting from a bearer. Requested name/expiry are retained and shown before approval; absent/mismatched echoes or actual key metadata are rejected before local credential storage.

Generated original challenge field retains explicit expiry/null, defaults to 30 days, and approval checks database-clock expiry before success. Existing serialization, domain authority, atomic audit, revocation/cancellation and token protection are preserved.

Cold route import exceeded its original first-test timeout and contaminated the following shared mock; bounded beforeAll setup now isolates the cold import. UI fixture receipt/status expectations and void cancellation mocks were corrected; raw failures remain archived.

Real built browser uses actual native cookies, migrated PostgreSQL, stale password proof, replacement session receipt, pending/approved token authentication and explicit second approval, then existing maintained TOTP/recovery/UV passkey lifecycles and rollback/non-replay controls. Virtual keys and fixture-owned injected failures are distinguished from physical authenticators.
limits: Complete password/email/destructive-action fences, operator bootstrap/break-glass and enterprise SSO/recovery remain open. No weaker fallback is added.
Complete source-aware read/effect lifetimes, native input receipts, original private-Memory/temporal/typed-origin failures, portability and remaining V10 requirements remain open.
Mixed-version server deployment, real provider/host/enterprise/manual accessibility qualification and latest full workspace release gates are not qualified.
This checkpoint is not complete V10, PR-ready, beta or production acceptance. No PR, merge or deployment was performed.
